To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the tidal acceleration in the direction of the principal null vector field is proportional to the square of the magnitude of the acceleration, and 2) the tidal acceleration perpendicular to the principal null vector is proportional to the magnitude of the principal null acceleration.
tidal accelerations are magnified by a factor of (1+3cos ^{2} θ)/4, where θ is the angle between the orbital plane and the principal null direction.
tidal accelerations are magnified in the limit that the orbit of the body is highly relativistic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the tidal accelerations of a test body in highly relativistic motion.
the tidal effects of a gravitational field on a test body moving in a highly relativistic orbit.
the kinematical effects which tidal forces exert upon test bodies in highly accelerated motion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tidal effects are negligible in general relativity for all astrophysical systems.

, in the case of a highly relativistic orbit preferentially aligned with repeated principal null rays, the tidal accelerations of test bodies are kinematically enhanced by a factor of 2 over the nonrelativistic case, while for orbits preferentially aligned in a direction orthogonal to the repeated principal null rays the tidal accelerations are kinematically diminished by a factor of (1/2).
the tidal accelerations in general, and in the case of the Kerr metric in particular, are very sensitive to the choice of the coordinates and of the frame field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tidal accelerations are magnified for bodies in orbits aligned with repeated principal null rays.
the tidal accelerations of a test body in a general spacetime are not necessarily the same as those in a flat spacetime.
we have found that the kinematical amplification of tidal acceleractions is a general phenomenon for all algebraically special spacetime geometries, including the Kerr metric.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tidal accelerations are kinematically magnified in general relativity, and this magnification is a function of the spacetime geometry.
, in general, tidal accelerations in general relativistic orbits are not simply related to those in Newtonian orbits.
tidal accelerations can be significantly enhanced by relativistic kinematical effects.
